content_units: Chart   What to plot   What it should show   Why it matters
Line chart: Monthly revenue trend   X-axis = month; Y-axis = total revenue   Jan   28,500  , Feb   30,500  , Mar   36,400     Shows overall growth momentum across the quarter

Stacked column chart: Revenue by month and product   X-axis = month; stacks = Standard vs Premium   Standard dominates each month, while Premium grows from   7,000   in Jan to   12,400   in Mar   Reveals product mix changes over time

Grouped bar chart: Region-product comparison   Bars for North/South split by Standard/Premium using quarter totals   North leads strongly in both products; South Premium appears only in Mar   Highlights concentration risk and whitespace in the South
- This makes the March Premium jump immediately visible.
- Best for showing where revenue is concentrated and where expansion potential exists.
1.   Revenue increased every month  , rising from   28,500   in January to   36,400   in March, a total gain of   27.7%   across the quarter.
2.   March was the strongest month  , contributing   38.2%   of total quarter revenue (36,400 out of 95,400).
3.   Standard is still the main revenue driver  , generating   68,400   total, or about   71.7%   of all revenue.
- Standard grew from   21,500   in Jan to   24,000   in Mar:   +11.6%
- Premium grew from   7,000   in Jan to   12,400   in Mar:   +77.1%
5.   South is underpenetrated in Premium  , with only   4,100   in the whole dataset and only appearing in   March  , while North Premium delivered   22,900   over the quarter.
